subject: Marginalized latent discrete chgpt for piecewise models - cause for concern?

messages.author: 2567ef0395c70306
messages.subject: Marginalized latent discrete chgpt for piecewise models - cause for concern?
parts:
I have some pathogen dieoff data for which I'm interested in removing initial periods of relatively stable population. I've thought to approach this by fitting a piecewise model, where mean log populations are distributed initially around a constant mean value, then eventually have a linear rate of decline after some changepoint:

data{
int Nobs;
vector[Nobs] ln_Conc;
vector[Nobs] sd_ln_Conc;
vector[Nobs] Time;
vector[Nobs] Obs; //Sample size for each observed concentration
}
//////////////////////////////////
transformed data{
real mu_Time;
real sd_Time;
real mu_Conc;
real sd_Conc;
real log_unif; //log uniform probability that end of maintenance period is any given point
vector[Nobs] C; //scaled natural log concentration
vector[Nobs] t; //scaled time
vector[Nobs] sd_C; //scaled sample standard deviations of ln concentration
vector[Nobs] SQRT_Obs;
vector[Nobs] mu_mu_maint;
mu_Time = mean(Time);
mu_Conc = mean(ln_Conc);
sd_Time = sd(Time);
sd_Conc = sd(ln_Conc);
log_unif = -log(Nobs);
C = ( ln_Conc - mu_Conc ) / sd_Conc;
t = Time / sd_Time;
sd_C = sd_ln_Conc / sd_Conc;
for (i in 1:Nobs){
mu_mu_maint[i] = mean(C[1:i]);
SQRT_Obs[i] = sqrt(Obs[i]);
}
}
//////////////////////////////////
parameters{
real mu_K;
real<lower=0> sd_K;
vector[Nobs-1] K_z;
real sd_mu_maint;
vector[Nobs] mu_maint_z;
}
///////////////////////////////////
transformed parameters{
vector[Nobs] mu_maint; //constant mean value for maintenance period
vector[Nobs-1] K_s; //scaled rate parameter for decay phases (one for each value of the changepoint)
vector[Nobs] lps; //log probability when marginalizing the changepoint of the maintenance phase
mu_maint = mu_mu_maint + sd_mu_maint * mu_maint_z;
K_s = mu_K + sd_K * K_z;
lps = rep_vector(log_unif, Nobs);
for (i in 1:(Nobs-1))
lps[i] = lps[i] + normal_lpdf(C[1:i] | mu_maint[i], sd_C[1:i] ./ SQRT_Obs[1:i]) + 
                              normal_lpdf(C[(i+1):Nobs] | mu_maint[i] - K_s[i] * (t[(i+1):Nobs] - t[i]), sd_C[(i+1):Nobs] ./ SQRT_Obs[(i+1):Nobs]);
lps[Nobs] = lps[Nobs] + normal_lpdf(C[1:Nobs] | mu_maint[Nobs], sd_C[Nobs]/SQRT_Obs[Nobs]);
}
///////////////////////////////////
model{

mu_K ~ normal(0, 1);
sd_K ~ student_t(3, 0, 1);
K_z ~ normal(0, 1);
sd_mu_maint ~ student_t(3, 0, 1);
mu_maint_z ~ normal(0,1);
target += log_sum_exp(lps);
}
////////////////////////////////////
generated quantities{
vector[Nobs-1] K;
real mu_M;
int CHGPT;
vector[Nobs] log_lik;
K = K_s * sd_Conc / sd_Time;

CHGPT = categorical_rng(softmax(lps));
mu_M = mu_maint[CHGPT] * sd_Conc + mu_Conc;
for (i in 1:Nobs){
log_lik[i] = normal_lpdf(ln_Conc[i] | i <= CHGPT ? mu_M : mu_M - K[min(CHGPT,Nobs-1)] * (Time[i] - Time[CHGPT]),
 sd_ln_Conc[i]/sqrt(Obs[i]));
}
}


When I run this model, I seem to get reasonable estimates of mu_M (the steady mean concentration before decay) and K, the linear rate of decay for the most probable value of the changepoint, which also seems reasonably estimated. However, the parameters for all other potential values of the changepoint are not well estimated, and have posterior distributions that essentially match the prior distributions. This raises some doubts for me as to whether the posterior probability of each value of the changepoint is well represented by the model runs. Should I be worried about using these results? Might there be a better way of specifying this model to accurately explore the posterior distribution?

On Tuesday, August 30, 2016 at 9:38:18 PM UTC-4, pcoll...@berkeley.edu wrote:
When I run this model, I seem to get reasonable estimates of mu_M (the steady mean concentration before decay) and K, the linear rate of decay for the most probable value of the changepoint, which also seems reasonably estimated. However, the parameters for all other potential values of the changepoint are not well estimated, and have posterior distributions that essentially match the prior distributions. These are some really deep questions. I could make some sweeping generalizations, but that isn't really useful. Would you mind asking your questions more precisely? 

For example, when you say "parameters for all other potential values of the changepoint are not well estimated," what do you mean? Why do you believe that? If the posterior distribution looks essentially like your prior distribution, why is that a bad thing? When you say "essentially," what do you mean?

Did you want to write a model that has some sort of property where those parameters are estimated well? Do you have enough data for that?

Anyway, if you're able to ask narrower questions, someone might be able to help.



Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Marginalized latent discrete chgpt for piecewise models - cause for concern?
parts:
Once you've defined the model, the posterior is whatever
you've defined. Stan helps you diagnose if you've accurately
reconstructed the posterior with R-hat and n_eff calculations.

You can try to debug your model code (in case you defined the
wrong posterior) by simulating data from your model and then
fitting it to ensure the model's well calibrated and recovering
the true parameters in the proper posterior intervals.

- Bob
